items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You should try walking after more meals to see how it affects you. Walking after dinner is linked to a rise in sugar about 18.3 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: None of your 16 scored dinners started at 8 pm or later. Keep it that way: across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a quarter of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Try to keep having dinner before 8 pm, as having dinner late is linked to sugar rising about 9.2 mg/dL more. This might help you feel better.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You're doing great with your overnight fast, averaging 14.0 hours and reaching 13 hours on 92.9% of nights. Keeping up this habit might be good for you.
